unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Present a complete and healthy study routine.

title: Warm Up
subtitle: Let's talk about study habits.
question: What do you usually do to stay focused and get your homework done at home?
starters: When I need to study, I usually...

title: Useful language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and example sentence for each word.
Ask the check question to confirm their understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: something you do regularly, often without thinking
words.example: Reading a book before bed is a good habit.
words.check: Which is a good study habit: checking your phone often or reviewing your notes?

words.definition: your usual way of doing things in a specific order
words.example: My morning routine includes waking up, eating breakfast, and walking to school.
words.check: What is the first thing you do in your morning routine?

words.definition: to give all your attention to one specific thing
words.example: I need a quiet room so I can focus on my homework.
words.check: Where is it easier to focus: in a noisy room or in a quiet library?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and example sentence for each word.
Ask the check questions to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.example: I study every day to improve my English.
words.check: If you improve your test score, does it go up or down?

words.example: I always do my homework in a quiet room.
words.check: Do you usually do your homework before or after dinner?

words.definition: to stop working for a short time to rest
words.example: I like to take a break and go outside for ten minutes.
words.check: When you take a break, do you keep studying or do you rest?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to finish your talk and give advice on your study routine.

linkers.use: to briefly summarize your main points
to share your top piece of advice

model: Well, I always do my homework early and take frequent breaks. To sum up, this routine really helps me improve. The best way is to find a quiet room where you can focus.

your_turn.teacher: Ask the student: What is the secret to building good study habits?
your_turn.student: Answer the teacher. End your response using 'In conclusion...' or 'The best way is to...'.

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine I'm your friend. I want to build a better study routine so I can get my homework done and still spend time with my family. Give me some advice using the phrases below.
student_guide: The best way to improve your focus is to ___.
A good study habit is to ___.
You should take a break when ___.
In conclusion, having a healthy routine is important because ___.

title: Real-world scenario
role_a: A student with a new, healthy study routine.
role_b: A mentor who wants to learn about the student's study habits.
problem: You need to explain your new study routine to your mentor and give advice on balancing schoolwork, family time, and rest.
mission: Explain your new habits for staying focused and completing homework effectively.
Share advice on how to balance schoolwork and family time.
Answer questions about taking breaks, managing weekends, and dealing with noisy rooms.
start: Hi there! I'd love to hear about your new study routine. So, how do you plan your day to improve your focus?

title: Wrap-up
recap: Vocabulary: habit, routine, focus, improve, do homework, take a break
Chunks: To sum up... / In conclusion... / The best way is to...
Skill: Presenting a complete and healthy study routine.
final_task: In one sentence, use a phrase like 'In conclusion...' to share your best advice for building a good study habit.
challenge: Write down your ideal weekend schedule using at least three of today's vocabulary words.
